18:34 Local Time, 05:34 GMT, 11:04 IST: Stump, Day 2 - A solid response from India to New Zealand's 368. When Nicholls and GP did that recovery act from 70/5, the Indians fans weren't overly positive about the batting, given the bowling prowess of NZ pace trio (Henry, Jamieson, Duffy). Facing them in their own backyard is tough but Jaiswal and KL put on a great show, after both were let off before Tea - they didn't review a plumb LBW for KL and GP put down Jaiswal at gully. Post Tea, the Indian openers pushed along nicely, with the former being the aggressor, playing delightful drives. He was racing from 60 to 70 to 80. He was heading to a certain hundred but a smart review from Henry and Co. (yes this time they listened to his adamance) got rid of Jaiswal against the run of play. KL got his first fifty against New Zealand to become the first Indian opener to get 50+ scores in all SENA countries. DDP has looked solid in his defence and is willing to dig deep.

Glenn Phillips (1/3): [You are the first man to score a century in all three formats against India in a calendar year. What does that sort of thing mean to you?] Obviously it's been a lot of time playing India this year. We've had great little stints against them and it's been a lot of fun getting out there trying to do some things with the boys. But obviously the way Toe (Henry Nicholls) batted today as well was fantastic. And it was good fight and effort from the boys all round. [How do you transfer that momentum through all three formats?] I suppose just try to change the game plan a little bit depending on what format we're in. Obviously ODI is slightly different from Test, which is obviously very different from T20. And I guess it's just going out there trying to keep things as simple as possible, watch the ball and, I guess, try and take it as long as possible for each format.

Phillips (2/3): [You're a very fast-paced athlete. You move quickly on the field. You do things quickly. Test match cricket, it's a little bit slower. How do you sort of slow yourself down or do you slow down?] I think it's about switching on and switching off. Obviously there is a lot of time in between balls to try and like just enjoy and I guess stay a little bit with the crowd and be aware of the fairies in between balls. And then coming back into it, trying to lock into everything that I do well and I guess trying to use that energy for the right time and the right purpose as possible. And sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn't. But obviously at the moment it's on a little bit of a roll, which is great.

Batting is expected to be easier as the day progresses and the ball gets old tomorrow. Can India get a healthy lead? Or will New Zealand hit back hard in the morning? We'll be up nice and early for all the Day 3 action. Good night!
